_comment: THE place to keep each step's container image download link (.sif), for
running workflows off-platform ('Deploy to my node'). Developers: edit this
file to add or replace a link; exports read it fresh every time, so no
restart is needed. Check your edit with:
cd backend && uv run python scripts/check_image_sources.py
Then add the link's ID (the part after /redeem/) to the allowlist in
.gitleaks.toml (repo root), or the PR's secret scan fails: it treats every postit
link as a secret until it is explicitly accepted there.
KEYS: the step's Tapis app id (tapis_app_id in its step.json) or its step
name (step_type_key). Case and -/_ are ignored, so 'few-shot-detection'
matches the app id 'few_shot_detection'. Prefer the app id: two steps can
share one app (custom_shapefile and heatmap do), and one key then covers
both.
WHAT A LINK IS USED FOR
* A step run by its Tapis app's container: the link to that .sif. The
deployment zip includes the file, the Deploy dialog shows the link, and
the runner downloads it once into --images-dir if it's missing.
* A step that ships its real container as an input (training, inference,
preprocessing): the link REPLACES the one in that step's step.json for
deployments, so a refreshed link only has to be changed here. Platform
runs still use step.json's own link; update both when it changes.
Tapis postit links are capability URLs: anyone holding one can download the
file, and they're copied into every exported bundle. Create them with high
(or unlimited) allowed uses and a long expiry, since every zip download and
every runner fetching a missing image redeems one use. Set WF_IMAGE_SOURCES
to another file's path to keep the links out of the repo.
